title: Auto-pin latch leak and safe-swap throttle mitigation
creator: Sofia Patel
description: During a regional canary-to-primary swap for the 'orca-13b' model, an automated pinning latch failed to clear for a subset of orchestrator workers. This left a small percentage (~3%) of traffic pinned to the old variant while the rest served the new variant; the mixed-serve triggered request-level throttles and autoscaler churn in downstream dedicated pools, leading to higher latency and a transient error-rate spike. This ticket tracks follow-ups: hardening the pin lifecycle, adding safety throttles to swaps, and reducing cross-region fanout during swaps.
timeline: 2025-10-30 09:12 UTC - Incident detected: Canary swap initiated, latency alarms tripped for region-eu-west-1.
2025-10-30 09:15 UTC - Pager oncall confirmed elevated 5xx rate and mixed-serve traces in tracing UI.
2025-10-30 09:25 UTC - Emergency rollback to previous stable variant completed; error rate decreased but autoscaler oscillation continued for 15 minutes.
2025-10-30 11:00 UTC - Initial RCA meeting: observed lingered pin state on 4/120 orchestrator workers; KV-sync timer jitter delayed clear messages.
2025-10-31 14:00 UTC - Engineering triage: identified race in pin-clear ack path when a worker restarts mid-swap.
2025-11-04 10:30 UTC - Small fix deployed to ensure idempotent pin-clear acknowledgement path (hotfix PR#1293).
2025-11-05 16:00 UTC - Canary of hotfix in staging passed; tox tests and a simulated partial-worker-restart scenario validated.
2025-11-08 09:00 UTC - This follow-up ticket opened to track remaining mitigations and operational controls.
impact_summary: ~3% of regional traffic experienced mixed-serve; average tail latency increased by ~120ms for affected requests and error-rate spiked to 4.7% for 18 minutes. No data-exfiltration or security impact. Some customers on dedicated pools saw autoscaling flaps and short-lived increased cost due to unnecessary scale-ups.
root_cause: A timing/race condition in the pin-clear acknowledgement path combined with KV-sync jitter and worker restart handling. When an orchestrator worker restarts during a swap, it could miss the in-flight clear message; the clearing logic was not fully idempotent and left stale pin metadata that reevaluated incorrectly under a concurrent routing fanout, producing mixed-serve state.
mitigations: Hotfix deployed: make pin-clear ack idempotent and durable (PR#1293).
Reconciler: add periodic scan that detects and clears stale pins older than 30s if they conflict with global version state. (short-term config change)
Introduce swap slow-start: progressive traffic ramp with a configurable throttle to cap swap-in rate per region to reduce autoscaler shock.
Add pre-swap readiness gate that validates KV-sync epoch match across >=99% of workers before cutover.
Improve observability: new metric 'pin_linger_seconds' and dashboard panels to show pin state per-worker and per-shard.
Failure-mode runbook: explicit steps to force-clear pins and a one-click rollback button in the Console for impacted rollouts.
